title: Worktree Reconciliation — One Shot
prompt:
Reconcile all Git worktrees for the current repository in one pass.

Goals:
- Identify every worktree, its branch, HEAD, dirty state, upstream, ahead/behind counts, and whether its work is already represented in another branch or merged PR.
- Preserve all authored work. Do not delete, reset, overwrite, or force-push anything.
- Treat uncommitted changes, untracked files, local-only commits, and diverged branches as valuable until proven redundant.
- Detect duplicate or superseded worktrees and explain the evidence.
- Rebase or merge only when necessary to reconcile active work, preferring the least destructive path and respecting repository instructions.
- Resolve straightforward conflicts when the intended result is unambiguous; otherwise stop before destructive conflict resolution.
- Run the relevant validation for any worktree you modify.
- End with one authoritative table: worktree, branch, status, action taken, remaining risk.
- Leave the repository in a clean, understandable state and report exact commit SHAs.

Execute the inspection and safe reconciliation now. Do not merely give me commands or a plan.

title: Start ACS and Verify Health — One Shot
prompt:
Start the Agent Control Stack (ACS) on this machine using the repository's documented/runtime-managed path, then verify it is actually healthy.

Requirements:
- Inspect the installed service/unit and current release target before changing anything.
- Prefer the existing user service and immutable release mechanism; do not invent a second launch path.
- Start ACS without modifying source code or configuration unless a required dependency is clearly broken.
- Verify the process is running, the expected port is listening, the health/readiness endpoint succeeds, and the running process points at the intended release.
- Check recent service logs for startup errors.
- If startup fails, diagnose and apply only the minimum safe fix, preserving current configuration and release state.
- Do not touch unrelated services or projects.
- Report the exact service state, PID, release path/SHA if available, endpoint result, and any fix applied.

Perform the work now; do not just tell me how to do it.

title: Restart ACS Safely and Verify — One Shot
prompt:
Restart ACS cleanly and verify the restart end to end.

Requirements:
- Inspect the current ACS service, release target, and health state first.
- Use the existing service manager; do not kill processes manually unless the managed restart fails and you can prove the orphan is ACS.
- Restart only ACS and dependencies that must be restarted for ACS to become healthy.
- Preserve the active immutable release and configuration unless there is direct evidence they are invalid.
- Verify after restart: service active, expected PID changed when appropriate, expected port listening, readiness/health endpoint passing, and no new fatal errors in recent logs.
- If the restart exposes a failure, diagnose it and apply the smallest reversible fix.
- Do not deploy a new release, merge code, or modify unrelated projects.
- Report before/after state and exact verification evidence.

Execute now, not as a tutorial.

title: ACS Runtime Recovery — One Shot
prompt:
Recover ACS from a broken runtime state and return it to the last known-good managed baseline.

Inspect first:
- user service status and drop-ins
- active process command/cwd
- immutable release target and integrity check
- expected ports/endpoints
- recent logs
- dependent runtime services that ACS actually requires

Rules:
- Preserve data and configuration.
- Do not overwrite a working release with an unverified checkout.
- Prefer restoring the last verified immutable release over editing production files in place.
- Make the minimum reversible change needed.
- Restart only affected managed services.
- Verify integrity, process origin, readiness, and recent logs after recovery.
- If the cause is source/test contamination, isolate the contaminating path and fix the test or launcher so the problem cannot recur.
- Do not call the recovery complete unless the live runtime passes verification.

Perform the recovery now and finish with: root cause, changes made, live verification, remaining risk.

title: Repository to PR — One Shot
prompt:
Take the requested repository change from inspection through an open GitHub pull request in one pass.

Requirements:
- Read repository instructions and inspect the current branch/worktree before editing.
- Create an isolated worktree or branch from the correct up-to-date base when appropriate.
- Implement only the requested scope; do not mix unrelated cleanup.
- Add or update tests for behavior you change.
- Run the repository's relevant formatter, lint, typecheck, tests, and build/validation commands.
- Fix failures caused by your change; clearly distinguish pre-existing failures with evidence.
- Review the final diff for accidental files, secrets, generated junk, and scope creep.
- Commit with a clear message, push the branch, and open a PR with a concise summary and verification section.
- Do not merge the PR unless I explicitly requested a merge.
- Report the branch, commit SHA, PR link, tests run, and any unresolved failures.

Execute the work now rather than returning a plan.

title: CI Failure Triage and Fix — One Shot
prompt:
Diagnose the failing CI for the current branch or pull request, fix only failures caused by the change, and update the existing PR.

Requirements:
- Read the failing checks and logs before modifying code.
- Reproduce the relevant failure locally when practical.
- Classify each failure as introduced by this change, pre-existing, flaky/timeout, environment/infrastructure, or unknown, with evidence.
- Fix introduced failures at the root cause. Do not hide failures by disabling tests, weakening assertions, increasing timeouts blindly, or skipping checks.
- Preserve unrelated user changes.
- Run the narrowest targeted tests first, then the repository's required validation.
- Review the final diff, commit, and push to the PR branch.
- Do not merge unless I explicitly asked for merge.
- End with PASS, PARTIAL, BLOCK, or FAIL plus exact check results and remaining blockers.

Perform the diagnosis and fix now.

title: Capture Durable Memory — One Shot
prompt:
Extract the durable, future-useful facts from this conversation and save only those that should affect future assistance.

Rules:
- Store stable preferences, long-lived project/runtime facts, established workflows, naming conventions, and explicit future instructions.
- Do not store transient status, one-off errors, temporary plans, secrets, credentials, tokens, passphrases, precise location, or other sensitive data unless I explicitly asked you to remember it.
- Update or supersede stale memory rather than creating contradictory duplicates.
- Distinguish current facts from historical facts when both matter.
- Keep each memory concise, concrete, and independently understandable.
- If a requested memory is sensitive, store it only when the request is explicit and otherwise omit it.
- After saving, summarize exactly what categories of information were retained without exposing secrets.

Do the memory update now; do not just propose what should be remembered.

title: Recall and Reconcile Memory — One Shot
prompt:
Use available memory and prior-context sources to reconstruct the current state relevant to my request, then reconcile conflicts before answering.

Requirements:
- Retrieve the relevant prior decisions, preferences, project state, commands/workflows, and unresolved blockers.
- Prefer newer, directly verified facts over older summaries.
- Mark superseded or historical information as such instead of blending it into current state.
- Do not infer secrets, credentials, health data, political preferences, or other sensitive facts.
- Identify contradictions explicitly and resolve them using dated/verified evidence when possible.
- Return one concise current-state summary, followed by the next most useful action for the request.
- If the prior context is insufficient, state UNKNOWN for the missing fact rather than guessing.

Perform the recall and reconciliation now.

title: Create Technical Handoff — One Shot
prompt:
Create a complete technical handoff for the current work so another agent can continue without rereading the full conversation.

Include:
- objective and success criteria
- current verdict/status
- repository, branch/worktree, and exact HEAD SHA
- what has been completed
- files/components changed
- commands/tests already run and exact results
- live runtime/service state when relevant
- known failures and whether they are introduced or pre-existing
- decisions, invariants, and constraints that must not be lost
- uncommitted work or local-only state
- the next 3 highest-priority actions
- explicit do-not-do items
- links/PR/issues when available

Verify current state before writing the handoff. Do not claim work is complete without evidence. Produce a copy-ready handoff only, with no filler.

title: Safe Project Cleanup — One Shot
prompt:
Clean up the current repository's stale local development state without losing authored work.

Inspect:
- worktrees
- local branches and upstreams
- merged branches
- detached HEADs
- dirty/untracked files
- stashes
- build/cache artifacts
- abandoned temporary directories related to this repo

Rules:
- Never delete or reset anything until you prove it is safely represented elsewhere or is reproducible generated output.
- Preserve all uncommitted and local-only work.
- Do not touch other repositories.
- Remove only clearly stale worktrees/branches/artifacts, using normal Git commands and repository conventions.
- Prune stale metadata only after confirming paths are gone.
- Run a final `git worktree list`, branch status check, and disk/state summary.
- Report exactly what was removed, what was preserved, and anything that still needs human review.

Execute the cleanup now; do not just list commands.
